title: The Army That Lost a War to Birds
style: Read this like a calm, deadpan British-style documentary narrator telling a ridiculous true story. Steady tone, unhurried, dry, never shouting. Small pauses before punchlines.

beats.vo: In 1932, the Australian army declared war on a bird. And lost.
It's late 1932 in Western Australia, and around twenty thousand emus have just walked out of the outback, straight into the wheat fields.
Many of these farmers fought in the First World War, so they ask the army for help.
The army sends three soldiers, two machine guns, and ten thousand bullets.
Day one, they spot fifty emus. The birds are out of range, and simply jog away.
Day three, a thousand emus walk up to a dam. The perfect ambush. Then the gun jams.
So they bolt a machine gun onto a truck. But emus can run thirty miles an hour, and the ride is so bumpy the gunner can't aim at anything.
Then the birds split into small groups, each with its own leader keeping watch.
After six days, the army retreats.
Luckily, they came back for a second try. Unluckily, so did the emus.
The major in charge reported that the birds could face machine guns like tanks.
Ever tried to catch one pigeon in a park? Now picture twenty thousand of them, six feet tall, that can outrun your truck.
After a month and nearly ten thousand bullets, the army claimed about a thousand emus. That's ten bullets per bird.
Farmers asked for the army again in 1934, 1943, and 1948. The answer was always no.
Today, the emu stands proudly on Australia's coat of arms. It was there before the war, too.

caption: In 1932 the Australian army went to war against emus. It did not go well. #history #emuwar #australia #didyouknow #animation
